ⓐ.summary: A species is a group of populations of individuals that are reproductively isolated from other groups and able to interbreed within the group.

ⓑ.summary: Woo's Triangle Model: through natural hybridization between different species within Brassica, chromosomes of one species are added to another, resulting in a new species possessing chromosomes from both.

c1.text: A species is a group of populations of individuals that are reproductively isolated from other groups, and able to interbreed within the group.

c2.text: Groups of organisms that are able to interbreed cannot be considered different species.

c3.text: Chinese cabbage (n=10) and cabbage (n=9) can interbreed to create rapeseed (n=19).

c4.text: Chinese cabbage and cabbage cannot be considered different species.

c5.text: According to Woo's Triangle Model (ⓑ), through natural hybridization between two different species within Brassica, the chromosomes of one species are added to those of another species, resulting in a new species possessing chromosomes from both.

c6.text: Chinese cabbage has n=10, cabbage has n=9, and black mustard has n=8.

c7.text: When black mustard and cabbage are hybridized, Ethiopian mustard is created.

c8.text: Ethiopian mustard has chromosome number n=17, which is the sum of chromosomes from black mustard (n=8) and cabbage (n=9).

c9.text: The number of chromosomes (n) in Ethiopian mustard is greater than the number of chromosomes (n) in black mustard.

c10.text: When Chinese cabbage and black mustard are hybridized, leaf mustard (n=18) is created as a new species possessing chromosomes from both.

c11.text: Black mustard and leaf mustard can be considered different species.

a.note: Ethiopian mustard has n=17 (8+9) according to ⓑ, which is greater than black mustard (n=8).

b.note: According to ⓐ, Chinese cabbage and cabbage interbreed so cannot be different species; according to ⓑ, leaf mustard is a new species synthesized from black mustard.

h1.text: A Maltese (n=39) and a Poodle (n=39), which are classified as the same species by ⓐ, produce a Maltipoo (n=39).

h2.text: The theory of species synthesis used in ⓑ classifies the Poodle and the Maltipoo as different species.

c.note: The theory of species synthesis in ⓑ requires hybridization between different species with added chromosomes; it does not apply to dogs of the same species with unchanged chromosome number, so ⓑ cannot build an argument for h2.
